sources.name: Official manufacturing project source — Intel
sources.excerpt: The U.S. Department of Commerce awarded Intel up to $7.865 billion in direct funding under the CHIPS and Science Act. This funding will support Intel’s expected U.S. investment of nearly $90 billion by the end of the decade, part of the company’s overall $100+ billion expansion plan, to expand capacity and capabilities at its sites in Arizona, New Mexico, Ohio, and Oregon. With this funding, Intel plans to develop a robust domestic semiconductor ecosystem, advancing U.S.-based leading-edge production. As previously announced and with the Department's support, Intel's overall expansion plan is estimated to support approximately 10,000 manufacturing jobs and 20,000 construction jobs across all four states.

sources.name: Official manufacturing project source — Texas Instruments
sources.excerpt: The U.S. Department of Commerce awarded Texas Instruments (TI) up to $1.61 billion in direct funding under the CHIPS and Science Act to strengthen domestic supply chain resilience, advance our national security, and bolster U.S. competitiveness in current-generation and mature-node semiconductor production. The funding would support TI’s investment of more than $18 billion through the end of decade for the construction of three state-of-the-art fabrication facilities, including two in Texas and one in Utah. The projects are estimated to create more than 2,000 manufacturing jobs and over 20,000 construction jobs over time.

sources.name: Official manufacturing project source — GlobalFoundries
sources.excerpt: The U.S. Department of Commerce awarded GlobalFoundries (GF) up to $1.587 billion in direct funding under the CHIPS and Science Act. The award will bolster U.S. competitiveness in current-generation semiconductor production by supporting the company’s capital investment of approximately $14 billion over the next 10-plus years in its U.S. manufacturing sites in New York and Vermont. The investment includes a new state-of-the-art facility in New York, the capability and capacity expansion of an existing facility in New York, and the modernization of the company’s operations in Vermont. The projects will create approximately 9,000 construction and 1,100 manufacturing jobs across both sites.

The investment includes a new state-of-the-art facility in New York, the capability and capacity expansion of an existing facility in New York, and the modernization of the company’s operations in Vermont. The projects will create approximately 9,000 construction and 1,100 manufacturing jobs across both sites.

sources.name: Official manufacturing project source — Intel
sources.excerpt: The U.S. Department of Commerce awarded Intel up to $7.865 billion in direct funding under the CHIPS and Science Act. This funding will support Intel’s expected U.S. investment of nearly $90 billion by the end of the decade, part of the company’s overall $100+ billion expansion plan, to expand capacity and capabilities at its sites in Arizona, New Mexico, Ohio, and Oregon. With this funding, Intel plans to develop a robust domestic semiconductor ecosystem, advancing U.S.-based leading-edge production. As previously announced and with the Department's support, Intel's overall expansion plan is estimated to support approximately 10,000 manufacturing jobs and 20,000 construction jobs across all four states.

sources.name: Official manufacturing project source — Micron
sources.excerpt: The U.S. Department of Commerce awarded Micron Technology Inc. (“Micron”), through its subsidiaries, Micron Idaho Semiconductor Manufacturing (TRITON), LLC and Micron New York Semiconductor Manufacturing LLC, direct funding under the CHIPS and Science Act. This funding will support Micron’s two-decade vision to invest approximately $100 billion in New York and $50 billion in Idaho, which will help the U.S. grow its share of advanced memory manufacturing from less than 2% today to approximately 10% by calendar year 2035. With this funding, Micron plans to expand the development and production of the most advanced memory semiconductor technology in New York and Idaho, which is expected to create approximately 23,000 direct jobs.

sources.name: Official manufacturing project source — Entegris
sources.excerpt: The Department of Commerce awarded Entegris up to $77 million in direct funding to support the construction of a state-of-the-art manufacturing center in Colorado Springs, Colorado. The center is being built in multiple phases: the first phase will support the production of Front Opening Unified Pods (FOUPs) and liquid filter membranes, and the second phase is expected to support the production of advanced liquid filters and fluid handling solutions. In addition to the manufacturing center, Entegris is committed to further expanding its R&D capabilities in the United States by the end of the decade. This investment will onshore critical semiconductor supply chain materials and solutions for leading-edge chip production.

sources.name: Official manufacturing project source — Intel
sources.excerpt: The U.S. Department of Commerce awarded Intel up to $7.865 billion in direct funding under the CHIPS and Science Act. This funding will support Intel’s expected U.S. investment of nearly $90 billion by the end of the decade, part of the company’s overall $100+ billion expansion plan, to expand capacity and capabilities at its sites in Arizona, New Mexico, Ohio, and Oregon. With this funding, Intel plans to develop a robust domestic semiconductor ecosystem, advancing U.S.-based leading-edge production. As previously announced and with the Department's support, Intel's overall expansion plan is estimated to support approximately 10,000 manufacturing jobs and 20,000 construction jobs across all four states.

(“Micron”), through its subsidiaries, Micron Idaho Semiconductor Manufacturing (TRITON) LLC and Micron New York Semiconductor Manufacturing LLC, direct funding under the CHIPS and Science Act. This funding will support Micron’s two-decade vision to invest approximately $100 billion in New York and $50 billion in Idaho, which will help the U.S. grow its share of advanced memory manufacturing from less than 2% today to approximately 10% by calendar year 2035. With this funding, Micron plans to expand the development and production of the most advanced memory semiconductor technology in New York and Idaho, which is expected to create approximately 23,000 direct jobs.

sources.name: Official manufacturing project source — Intel
sources.excerpt: The U.S. Department of Commerce awarded Intel up to $7.865 billion in direct funding under the CHIPS and Science Act. This funding will support Intel’s expected U.S. investment of nearly $90 billion by the end of the decade, part of the company’s overall $100+ billion expansion plan, to expand capacity and capabilities at its sites in Arizona, New Mexico, Ohio, and Oregon. With this funding, Intel plans to develop a robust domestic semiconductor ecosystem, advancing U.S.-based leading-edge production. As previously announced and with the Department's support, Intel's overall expansion plan is estimated to support approximately 10,000 manufacturing jobs and 20,000 construction jobs across all four states.

(GlobalWafers), of up to $406 million to support the construction of new wafer manufacturing facilities in Sherman, Texas and St. Peters, Missouri. Approximately 90% of silicon wafers are sourced from East Asia today, with five corporations managing the majority of global supply – GlobalWafers is one of the five global leaders in this market. sources.excerpt: The U.S. Department of Commerce awarded Samsung Austin Semiconductor, LLC, a subsidiary of Samsung Electronics (Samsung), up to $4.745 billion in direct funding under the CHIPS and Science Act to strengthen the resilience of the U.S. semiconductor supply chain, advance U.S. technology leadership, and fuel U.S. global competitiveness. Samsung – the only leading-edge semiconductor company that is a leader in both advanced memory and advanced logic technologies – is expected to invest over $37 billion dollars in the region in the coming years, and the investment would support the creation of over 15,000 jobs.

sources.name: Official manufacturing project source — Polar
sources.excerpt: The U.S. Department of Commerce awarded Polar Semiconductor (Polar) up to $123 million in total direct funding under the CHIPS and Science Act to expand and modernize the company’s manufacturing facility in Bloomington, Minnesota, which is expected to almost double its U.S. production capacity of sensor and power chips within two years. The CHIPS incentive award catalyzes an investment of more than $525 million from private, state, and federal sources to transform Polar from a majority foreign-owned in-house manufacturer to a majority U.S.-owned commercial foundry, expanding opportunities for U.S. chip designers to innovate and produce technologies domestically. Through Polar’s semiconductor manufacturing operations, the investment is expected to create over 160 manufacturing and construction jobs in Minnesota.

sources.name: TeraWulf: Kentucky PSC approves Justified RESA
sources.excerpt:
TeraWulf Inc. (Nasdaq: WULF) (“TeraWulf” or the “Company”), a vertically integrated owner, developer and operator of large-scale digital infrastructure, today announced that the Kentucky Public Service Commission (“PSC”) has approved the Retail Electric Service Agreement (“RESA”) supporting up to 482 megawatts (“MW”) of electric service for TeraWulf’s Justified Data Campus in Hancock County, Kentucky. The approval represents an important milestone for Justified and, in TeraWulf’s view, validates a strong model for responsible large-scale data center development: securing substantial power capacity while ensuring that project-specific costs and risks are borne by the large-load customer, protecting existing ratepayers and creating incremental value for utilities and local communities. In its August 21, 2026 order, the Commission concluded: “After consideration of the entire record, the Commission finds that the proposed RESA contains adequate protections for existing customers, appropriately allocates financial and operational risks, establishes rates that are fair, just and reasonable, and provides for adequate and reliable service.” Under the approved structure, TeraWulf is responsible for the market, transmission, delivery and other costs attributable to serving its load, together with customer-specific infrastructure costs and substantial credit-support obligations.
[…]
The agreement also includes negotiated demand adders and customer charges that provide incremental contributions to Big Rivers Electric Corporation (“Big Rivers”) and Kenergy Corp.
[…]
The Justified Data Campus is being developed at the former Century Aluminum Hawesville facility, where approximately 482 MW of existing transmission capability remains available following the closure of the aluminum smelter.

sources.name: TeraWulf: Kentucky PSC approves Justified RESA
sources.excerpt:
TeraWulf Inc. (Nasdaq: WULF) (“TeraWulf” or the “Company”), a vertically integrated owner, developer and operator of large-scale digital infrastructure, today announced that the Kentucky Public Service Commission (“PSC”) has approved the Retail Electric Service Agreement (“RESA”) supporting up to 482 megawatts (“MW”) of electric service for TeraWulf’s Justified Data Campus in Hancock County, Kentucky. The approval represents an important milestone for Justified and, in TeraWulf’s view, validates a strong model for responsible large-scale data center development: securing substantial power capacity while ensuring that project-specific costs and risks are borne by the large-load customer, protecting existing ratepayers and creating incremental value for utilities and local communities. In its August 21, 2026 order, the Commission concluded: “After consideration of the entire record, the Commission finds that the proposed RESA contains adequate protections for existing customers, appropriately allocates financial and operational risks, establishes rates that are fair, just and reasonable, and provides for adequate and reliable service.” Under the approved structure, TeraWulf is responsible for the market, transmission, delivery and other costs attributable to serving its load, together with customer-specific infrastructure costs and substantial credit-support obligations.
[…]
The agreement also includes negotiated demand adders and customer charges that provide incremental contributions to Big Rivers Electric Corporation (“Big Rivers”) and Kenergy Corp.
[…]
The Justified Data Campus is being developed at the former Century Aluminum Hawesville facility, where approximately 482 MW of existing transmission capability remains available following the closure of the aluminum smelter.

sources.excerpt: Today, OG&E, the operating subsidiary of locally-headquartered OGE Energy Corp. (NYSE: OGE), announced that it will power three new data centers that Google announced in Muskogee and Stillwater last year. The data centers and associated Electric Service Agreements will provide economic growth for local communities and the state, contribute to grid stability, and benefit OG&E's current customers. As technology continues to propel industry and our personal lives forward, OG&E will power the 21st century economy through these agreements with Google, whose data centers power key services that billions of people use every day, from online banking to hospital records to 911 systems. OG&E worked closely with Google to secure broad customer protections for years to come. Under this agreement, Google is committing to pay 100% of the costs to connect the data center sites to the grid as well as all contracted costs regardless of the company's energy use. Google will also pay its share of power generation required to serve these data centers. "OG&E is pleased to support Google and together advance growth in our home state, ensuring our current customers benefit from data center expansion that meets the technology needs of the 21st century economy at some of the lowest rates in the country," said Sean Trauschke, Chairman, President and CEO of OGE Energy Corp. "This unique agreement is a model for future data center partnerships and forms the basis for a new large-load The Electric Service Agreements and Capacity Purchase Agreements will be filed for review with the Oklahoma Corporation Commission in the coming days. The OCC must formally approve the agreement between OG&E and Google to supply power to the data center sites. sources.name: Entergy Arkansas: Google West Memphis power service agreement
sources.excerpt:
Google is good for Arkansas
  and great for Entergy customers
  Google is investing $4 billion on cloud and artificial intelligence infrastructure in
  Arkansas, including the development of a new data center in West Memphis
  – the company’s first facility in the state – powered by Entergy.
  Their historic investment in our state is bringing unparalleled benefits that will
  improve the lives of Arkansans for generations to come.


How will it benefit you?
           High tech partner = Lower cost power
           Google will cover the full energy costs associated with powering the facility, which will produce more
           than $1 billion in net customer savings over the life of the contract. In addition, as a new large industrial
           customer on our grid, Google will pick up more of the grid maintenance improvement costs that existing
           customers would otherwise have to bear alone and at a larger share than residential and small
           business customers.
           Adding any power-intensive facility to our grid can raise questions about its impact on service reliability
           for other customers, but we’ve ensured that our power service agreement with Google not only protects
           reliability for all customers, it improves it through measures such as:
           • Adding a new solar generation and battery storage facility in Jefferson County financially supported
             by Google.
           • Electrical infrastructure additions and improvements that will enhance reliability of the entire grid and
             lower costs for all customers.
           • A program to reduce data center power use during peak hours to support grid stability for all customers.

sources.name: Microsoft Hebron datacenter construction update
sources.excerpt: Hebron datacenter construction update Microsoft is building a datacenter in Hebron, Ohio. Why datacenters are needed Datacenters provide the physical infrastructure for the technology we depend on at work and in our personal lives. Whenever you open an app on your phone, join a virtual classroom or meeting, snap and save photos, or play a game with your friends online, you are using a datacenter. Local businesses, government, hospitals, and schools rely on datacenters every day to deliver goods and services to you. Construction update—July 2026 Summer construction activities continue at the Hebron datacenter site Summer construction continues at the Microsoft datacenter site in Hebron, with crews focused on long-term site development, safety, and environmental protection. Work on the substation is also expected to get underway. Residents may notice permanent and temporary fencing, construction of stormwater holding ponds, ongoing erosion control maintenance, and fill material being brought to the site for grading. Truck traffic through the summer and into the fall will vary based on construction needs, and crews will continue working to minimize impacts on nearby roads and properties. Microsoft and its construction partners remain committed to keeping the community informed; questions or concerns can be directed to 740-235-2678 or info@MSFTHebronDatacenter.com . Construction update—May 2026 As site preparation work continues, some Sunday work may be necessary to keep the project on schedule due to weather delays and time-sensitive construction milestones. Ames Construction remains in close communication with the Village of Hebron, which reviews and approves all work schedules and any temporary adjustments to permitted work hours. To receive advance notice of changes to work hours and other project updates, please send your email address to the project team at info@MSFTHebronDatacenter.com . Construction update—March 2026 Site preparation begins at Hebron datacenter site In the coming weeks, neighbors will begin to see initial activity on the site. Work will start with the removal of trees along the perimeter. Felled trees will be staged on site and processed with a woodchipper at a later date. Some logs may be removed from the site for reuse. The walking trail in the adjacent Thomas J. Evans Park may be closed briefly for safety reasons as trees are removed. Equipment used during tree removal will include chainsaws, large trucks, forestry-industry heavy equipment, and woodchippers. Crews will access the site using a temporary construction entrance off Canyon Road. A permanent construction access road will be established on the east side of the property, adjacent to the industrial park for continued work. The tree removal activity is expected to last approximately one week, not counting the wood chipping at a later date. We expect early site preparation to be completed by the end of the year with vertical construction to follow. We will share more details on this timeline as soon as they are available. We encourage neighbors to check back regularly for updates as work progresses. For questions or concerns, please contact the Ames project team at 740-235-2678 or email info@MSFTHebronDatacenter.com . Construction update – February Mass grading construction is estimated to begin in February and completed in November 2026. Together with our general contractor AMES Construction, we will keep neighbors informed in advance of construction work. Completion of construction does not indicate datacenter operation/availability. Construction overview Microsoft has contracted AMES Construction as the general contractor for the Hebron datacenter in Ohio. Construction hours Permitted construction hours are Monday to Friday 7:00 AM – 7:00 PM with Saturdays and occasional Sundays from 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM. Staying connected We will keep the community up to date via our Ohio page on the Microsoft in Your Community blog . For construction related questions, email AMES at info@MSFThebrondatacenter.com or leave a message at 1-740-235-2678. For community-related questions, email us at ColumbusDC@microsoft.com or leave a message at 1-513-301-1414.

sources.name: Microsoft Hickory datacenter construction update
sources.excerpt: Hickory datacenter construction update Microsoft is building a datacenter in the greater Hickory, North Carolina area, near the Hickory-Lincolnton Highway in Catawba County. Why datacenters are needed Datacenters provide the physical infrastructure for the technology we depend on at work and in our personal lives. Whenever you open an app on your phone, join a virtual classroom or meeting, snap and save photos, or play a game with your friends online, you are using a datacenter. Local businesses, government, hospitals, and schools rely on datacenters every day to deliver goods and services to you. May 2026: Construction update Construction activity continues to progress at the Hickory datacenter site in North Carolina. Underground utilities installation is underway across the west, north, and south areas of the site. This work includes sanitary systems, water distribution, fire infrastructure, telecommunications, and stormwater systems that support overall site development. Foundation work is also in progress. The project remains on track to begin steel structure installation at the end of June, marking the next major phase of construction. February 2026: Construction update At the Hickory/Stover site, the general contractor Clayco will begin initial site setup and earthwork activities. This phase focuses on preparing the site for future construction and does not involve vertical building at this time. Construction hours Construction activity is expected to take place from Monday to Saturday, 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM. Work hours will follow local permitting requirements. October 2024: Community information session We have rescheduled the community information session : Monday, October 21, 5:30 PM – 7:00 PM at the Stover Datacenter Site, Hickory Lincolnton Hwy, Newton NC . September 2024: Construction update ***Meeting postponed due to recent hurricane devastation *** We invite you to a community information session: Monday, September 30, 5:00 PM – 7:00 PM at Rhoney’s Chapel AME Zion Church, 3778 Hickory Lincolnton Hwy, Newton, NC 28258 Construction timeline Datacenter construction began in July 2024. The general contractor Ames Construction Company is preparing the site by excavating and crushing rock onsite. In some cases, this involves controlled rock excavation and fracturing in the early afternoon to break apart larger rocks. Together with our general contractor Ames Construction Company, we will keep neighbors informed in advance of construction work. Staying connected We will keep the community up to date via our North Carolina page in our Microsoft in your community blog. As of March 2026, our general contractor is Clayco. For construction related questions, email Thomas Plant at plantt@claycorp.com or leave a message at 919-810‑3035. If you have any additional questions, please contact the Microsoft Community Engagement Manager at northcarolinadc@microsoft.com or leave a voicemail at 980-776-2251.

sources.name: Microsoft Maiden-Boyd Farms datacenter construction update
sources.excerpt: Maiden-Boyd Farms datacenter construction update Microsoft is constructing the Boyd Farms datacenter. The datacenter construction site is located off Zeb Haynes Road in Maiden, North Carolina. Why datacenters are needed Datacenters provide the physical infrastructure for the technology we depend on at work and in our personal lives. Whenever you open an app on your phone, join a virtual classroom or meeting, snap and save photos, or play a game with your friends online, you are using a datacenter. Local businesses, government, hospitals, and schools rely on datacenters every day to deliver goods and services to you. Construction update May 2026 Microsoft continues construction at the Boyd Farm datacenter site, with crews making steady progress across building foundations, underground utilities, and infrastructure installation. The general contractor for this site changed to Clark Construction. Crews are advancing electrical, underground utility, and slab work, with the first slab pour planned for early June. South entrance utilities—including sewer, stormwater, water, and fire protection—are nearing completion. Campus-wide underground utility work continues through July, with electrical vault installation planned from early June through mid-August. Telecommunications and medium-voltage infrastructure work continues in future development areas into late summer. Rock removal update Testing to understand underground rock conditions is complete, and teams are reviewing the results to plan next steps. Additional work may be needed to remove rock in certain areas, and this request is currently under review. If approved, crews may use controlled blasting to safely break apart underground rock as part of site preparation. This work will follow all safety requirements, and neighbors will be notified in advance. Rock removal activities, including breaking, removing, and filling areas, are expected to take about 2–3 months once work begins. Construction timeline Datacenter construction began April 1, 2024. The general contractor Morgan Construction Company is preparing the site by clearing and grading it. From there they will move into excavation work and continue construction through the spring of 2025. Together with our general contractor Morgan Construction Company, we will keep neighbors informed in advance of construction work. Staying connected We will keep the community up to date via our North Carolina page in our Microsoft in your community blog. For daily operational questions, you can also reach out to the contractor at boydfarms@clarkconstruction.com , phone 828-270-1600.

If approved, crews may use controlled blasting to safely break apart underground rock as part of site preparation. This work will follow all safety requirements, and neighbors will be notified in advance. Rock removal activities, including breaking, removing, and filling areas, are expected to take about 2–3 months once work begins. Construction timeline Datacenter construction began April 1, 2024. The general contractor Morgan Construction Company is preparing the site by clearing and grading it. From there they will move into excavation work and continue construction through the spring of 2025. Together with our general contractor Morgan Construction Company, we will keep neighbors informed in advance of construction work. Staying connected We will keep the community up to date via our North Carolina page in our Microsoft in your community blog. For daily operational questions, you can also reach out to the contractor at boydfarms@clarkconstruction.com , phone 828-270-1600.

sources.name: Microsoft Tyrone datacenter update
sources.excerpt: Tyrone datacenter update Project overview Microsoft is planning to build a new datacenter in Tyrone. In line with Microsoft’s Datacenter Community Pledge , our work follows the Community-First Infrastructure approach, reflecting a long term commitment to responsibility, transparency, and partnership with the communities where our datacenters operate. Why datacenters are needed Datacenters provide the physical infrastructure for the technology we depend on at work and in our personal lives. Whenever you open an app on your phone, join a virtual classroom or meeting, snap and save photos, or play a game with your friends online, you are using a datacenter. Local businesses, government, hospitals, and schools rely on datacenters every day to deliver goods and services to you. Investing in cloud and AI infrastructure in Georgia supports long-term digital growth and helps ensure that essential online services remain reliable and accessible. Recap of the community information session – May 2026 Thank you for joining us at the information session. If you were not able to attend, we have posted a link to view the boards that were shared and answers to frequently asked questions below: Board s and slideshow from the Tyrone community meeting Understanding water use at Microsoft datacenters Understanding energy use at Microsoft datacenters Increasing access to digital skills and local job opportunities Frequently asked questions Community information session—May 2026 Please join us for a Town of Tyrone community information session on Tuesday, May 19, 2026, from 4 PM to 7 PM at the Town Hall, 950 Senoia Road, Tyrone, GA 30290. The format is an open house with topical stations that include the following (subject to change): Town priorities and entitlement process overview Energy Water and sustainability Construction timeline and impacts Site design (noise, aesthetics, trees, and emissions) Community investments/ engagement and workforce pathways Operations and jobs What to expect next / how to stay engaged Staying connected We will keep the community up to date via our Georgia page on the Microsoft in Your Community blog . For community-related questions, email georgiadc@microsoft.com or leave a message at 470-832-6713. For media inquiries, please reach out to rapidresponse@we-worldwide.com .

sources.name: Microsoft HR Ranch Road datacenter construction
sources.excerpt: HR Ranch Road datacenter construction Microsoft is building a datacenter on HR Ranch Road located in the greater Cheyenne, WY area. Why datacenters are needed Datacenters provide the physical infrastructure for the technology we depend on at work and in our personal lives. Whenever you open an app on your phone, join a virtual classroom or meeting, snap and save photos, or play a game with your friends online, you are using a datacenter. Local businesses, government, hospitals, and schools rely on datacenters every day to deliver goods and services to you. Construction overview Microsoft has contracted with JE Dunn as the general contractor for HR Ranch Road construction site in Cheyenne, WY. Construction is expected to continue for approximately 18–24 months, with heavy earthwork anticipated from July 2025 through November 2025 and overall completion targeted for early 2026. Completion of construction does not indicate datacenter operation/availability. Construction will take place Monday through Saturday, 7:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. Neighbors within the vicinity will be notified ahead of construction. A community meeting is planned for November 2025. Staying connected We will keep the community up to date via our Cheyenne page in our Microsoft in Your Community blog. For construction related questions, please contact Project Manager (PM): Jake Coutts, HRRanch@jedunn.com . For community related questions, contact us at CheyenneDC@microsoft.com . For PR-related questions, contact the Microsoft Media Relations at rapidresponse@we-worldwide.com .

sources.name: Microsoft East Point datacenter project overview
sources.excerpt: East Point datacenter project overview Learn more about Microsoft’s work in East Point, Georgia Thank you for your cooperation and patience as we continue construction on the buildout of the datacenter campus. We are committed to providing you with regular updates and communication through this website. Visit our photo gallery of the project What is a datacenter? Datacenters are part of everyday life Essential for modern technology, datacenters power everything from online grocery shopping, online banking, and remote work to scheduling medical appointments and staying connected with family and friends. Datacenters also support businesses, hospitals, schools, and governments. Datacenter buildings house thousands of computer servers and data storage devices connected to the internet. Video: Learn more about datacenters Datacenter virtual tour East Point datacenter project at a glance The project includes the construction of two datacenter buildings, a power substation, privacy screening, support facilities, and landscaping. Total Parcels: 6 Parcels Combined acreage: 131.6 (Developed Acreage 84.6) No. of Buildings : 2 Buildings Building Square footage: 489,370 sq ft. (244,685 x 2) Parking Spaces: 114 spaces Total # of Employees: +/- 50 per Building Neighborhood enhancements around the datacenter The datacenter project will also include the following neighborhood additions: A nature walk area accessible from Ben Hill Road and will include a walking trail, native plants and trees, and seating. Three-quarters of an acre in size (33,000 square feet), with dimensions of 75 feet by 440 feet. Our proposed vegetation will include a native/ sustainable mixture of evergreen and deciduous trees to be installed along Ben Hill Road. Preview the nature walk with this virtual tour. Sidewalks along Ben Hill Road An 8-10 ft. solid barrier privacy wall and supplemental trees for additional buffering between the datacenter and residential homes. Neighbors directly impacted unanimously chose this screening option. Updated landscaping along Ben Hill Road. Microsoft will plant mature and faster-growing trees, at least 18-22 ft. in height along Ben Hill Road to further screen the datacenter campus and allow it to blend into the surrounding environment naturally. Work at the datacenter We believe economic growth can and must be inclusive. That’s why we invest to help individuals, organizations, and communities access pathways to growth and opportunity. Working with local organizations and leaders, we invest in programs to help people build skills for jobs and livelihood opportunities and increase access to computer science education. Join our team. Explore our resources and build the skills to work at a datacenter Take a look at the career opportunities in Georgia The Microsoft Datacenter Academy is coming to the Atlanta Technical College. Project resources Stay informed about our ongoing East Point datacenter project updates Project timing: 2023-2026 Phase: Construction Learn more about our most frequently asked questions about datacenters Stay connected Contact us by calling 470-832-6713 or via email us at eastpointdc@microsoft.com Stop by our booth and visit us this summer at the Wednesday Wind Down event which will recur on fourth Wednesday between May through August, from 5 to 9 p.m. Community investments Microsoft invests in local programs that benefit people of all ages. In Greater Atlanta, our collaborations are organized by our focus areas of Skills for Jobs, Enabling Sustainability, and Empowering Communities. Read about many of our community investments across Greater Atlanta since 2022. Technology Education and Learning Support (TEALS) is a Microsoft Philanthropies program that builds sustainable computer science (CS) programs in high schools. We focus on serving students excluded from learning CS because of race, gender, or geography. Microsoft is building a datacenter campus in East Point, Georgia The project includes the construction of two datacenter buildings, a power substation, privacy screening, support facilities, and landscaping. Flip through our photo gallery to see the architectural renderings of the project and a computer animated preview video of the nature walk on Ben Hill Road. Learn more in our project overview section. Datacenter entrance off of Ben Hill Road Rendering of mature trees and sidewalk looking North on Ben Hill Road. Aerial rendering of datacenter campus and retaining wall location Ben Hill Road pocket park nature walk details Watch a rendering animation of the future Ben Hill Road nature walk

sources.name: Microsoft Wiseman Boulevard datacenter construction update
sources.excerpt: Wiseman Boulevard datacenter construction update Microsoft is building a datacenter on Wiseman Boulevard in San Antonio, Texas. Why datacenters are needed Datacenters provide the physical infrastructure for the technology we depend on at work and in our personal lives. Whenever you open an app on your phone, join a virtual classroom or meeting, snap and save photos, or play a game with your friends online, you are using a datacenter. Local businesses, government, hospitals, and schools rely on datacenters every day to deliver goods and services to you. Construction overview Microsoft and its general contractor Walbridge Aldinger LLC have begun construction on the Wiseman Boulevard datacenter in San Antonio. Construction is estimated to be complete in March 2026. Completion of construction does not indicate datacenter operation/availability. Our general contractor, Walbridge Aldinger LLC, will continue to mitigate dust around the site. They anticipate landscaping and asphalt roadways to be complete by early fall 2023. Construction hours Monday – Friday 7:00am – 8:00pm Saturday 8:00am – 8:00pm Sunday 9:00am – 5:00pm If construction falls outside of normal operating hours, our team will notify the homeowners association via email 72 hours in advance as stated in the San Antonio city code. Staying connected We will keep the community up to date via our Microsoft in your community page at https://local.microsoft.com/texas . For construction related questions, please contact Paul Acevedo at 210-729-8325 Community-related questions can be sent to texasDC@microsoft.com For PR-related questions, contact the Microsoft Media Relations at rapidresponse@we-worldwide.com

sources.name: Microsoft Responsible development in Prince William County
sources.excerpt: Responsible development in Prince William County An update on our environmental work at the proposed Wellington datacenter site In 2024, Microsoft purchased land in Prince William County, Virginia for the purpose of datacenter development. While datacenter development has yet to commence, we have started the process of applying for permits. The project remains in the early planning and permitting stage with actual datacenter construction still a long way off. Microsoft is committed to responsible development on this site, respecting the unique and challenging environmental history of this land. We’re working with local partners to carry out all necessary environmental remediation and ensure our future plans have appropriately considered the local context and adequately protect the community from future environmental degradation. This environmental work is the reason that we’ve started the planning and permitting process so early – taking the necessary time to ensure plans are advanced responsibly, in compliance with all federal, state and local regulations. The approximately 124-acre property is located on Wellington Road in Gainesville, Virginia, and has a history of industrial use that predates Microsoft’s ownership and resulted in soil and groundwater contamination. Cleanup of this pre-existing contamination continues under a longstanding U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) consent order, which outlines the cleanup requirements and mandates ongoing reporting to the EPA. Under government oversight, the prior industrial operator remains responsible for maintaining the site’s groundwater treatment and monitoring systems and addressing the contamination. Microsoft is funding and providing technical support to relocate and modernize the treatment infrastructure so cleanup can continue as property plans advance. Microsoft and the previous industrial operator are coordinating with the EPA, the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality, Prince William County, and other agencies to ensure that our plans comply with all existing regulations and any necessary environmental reviews and approvals are completed before any work moves forward. Additional information about the property’s cleanup history can be found here: EPA RCRA ID: VAD023741705 | US EPA As plans are developed, Microsoft’s approach will be to avoid and minimize impacts on wetlands, waterways, and other natural resources. If impacts cannot be avoided, appropriate permits would be sought, and mitigation measures such as funding for stream and wetland restoration would be incorporated into the project. As construction moves forward, environmental controls will address stormwater, erosion, soil, dust, and waste. Additionally, materials will be evaluated and managed in accordance with applicable requirements. We will continue to share updates with the local community as plans advance and key milestones are reached.

sources.name: Microsoft Microsoft breaks ground on La Porte datacenter project
sources.excerpt: Microsoft breaks ground on La Porte datacenter project On Thursday, June 18, Microsoft marked an important milestone in La Porte, Indiana, with a groundbreaking event for its new datacenter project, alongside local leaders and community partners. In addition to the datacenter groundbreaking, Microsoft celebrated the signing of a partnership with Ivy Tech Community College to launch its first Microsoft Datacenter Academy in Indiana. The event brought together elected officials, community stakeholders, and partners to highlight progress on site development and reinforce Microsoft’s commitment to investing in the region through jobs, infrastructure, and long-term community engagement. Brad Smith, Microsoft Vice Chair and President, delivered remarks as part of Microsoft’s Community-First Infrastructure initiative, joining the La Porte mayor and local leaders. “AI infrastructure is driving demand for skilled trades nationwide,” said Smith. “We’re committed to helping fill these jobs with people in the communities where we operate. Our Datacenter Academy agreement with Ivy Tech Community College will do just that by equipping people in Indiana with the skills to pursue the jobs we will create here.” Beyond the thousands of construction jobs, the first phase of the new datacenter is expected to create more than 600 permanent Microsoft jobs. It will grow local tax revenues to support schools and the broader community for generations. The campus will be designed with the latest energy efficient and closed-loop liquid cooling technologies to conserve natural resources. And Microsoft will enhance the surrounding ecosystem to strengthen flood protection and natural habitat.

sources.name: Microsoft Malaga datacenter project overview
sources.excerpt: Malaga datacenter project overview Project overview Microsoft is developing a datacenter campus on Malaga-Alcoa Highway. The project is currently in the first phase of development. Construction of the first datacenter will begin in June 2023 and is expected to conclude in early 2026. Completion of construction does not indicate datacenter operation/availability. The timing of construction of the other two datacenter buildings will be driven by customer demand for Microsoft cloud services. Malaga datacenter construction update Microsoft will begin construction for the first phase of development of the Malaga datacenter in June 2023. The datacenter construction site is located on Malaga-Alcoa Highway in Malaga, Washington. Why datacenters are needed Datacenters provide the physical infrastructure for the technology we depend on at work and in our personal lives. Whenever you open an app on your phone, join a virtual classroom or meeting, snap and save photos, or play a game with your friends online, you are using a datacenter. Local businesses, government, hospitals, and schools rely on datacenters every day to deliver goods and services to you. Construction timeline Datacenter construction will begin in June 2023. The general contractor will begin clearing the site, which includes demolishing some existing buildings. From there, construction of the buildings is expected to commence in May 2024 and last through early 2026. Construction completion of the datacenter buildings does not indicate operability. For this clearing phase of construction, work is expected to take place from Monday through Friday between 6:30 AM and 4:30 PM, with occasional work as needed on Saturdays during the same hours. We will keep neighbors informed in advance of construction work and perform work at less disruptive times when possible (after hours in industrial areas and during daytime hours in residential areas). Additionally, our general contractor will use water trucks to mitigate dust. Staying connected For more information about Microsoft’s work in Central Washington, visit the Microsoft in your community page. For community-related questions, contact us at CentralWaDC@microsoft.com or leave a voicemail at 1-509-794-6526. For PR-related questions, contact Microsoft Media Relations. March 29, 2023 community info session recap Microsoft hosted a community information session about the planned Malaga datacenter campus on March 29, 2023. The project is in the planning and permitting stage for the first phase of development, which will include one datacenter building, substation, water tanks, fencing, landscaping, and other support facilities. The meeting opened with remarks from Lisa Karstetter, Community Manager for Microsoft; Ron Cridlebaugh, incoming Economic Director for Chelan County; Jim Kuntz, Chief Executive Officer for Chelan Douglas Regional Port Authority; and Shawn Smith, Managing Director of Energy Resources for Chelan County PUD. Microsoft appreciated the opportunity to talk with the more than 110 community members that participated in the meeting and visited stations to talk with subject matter experts. The meeting stations focused on an overview of datacenters, the current plan for the Malaga datacenter campus (for example, site plan, water, energy), next steps for permitting and construction, and Microsoft’s partnerships in the community. In talking with community members, Microsoft, Chelan County PUD, and Malaga Water District heard comments and responded to questions about water, construction timeline, power for the site, traffic, jobs, and community investments. If you were unable to attend the community info session, you can also view the boards shown at the meeting. English information session boards Spanish information session boards March 2023: information session invitation Join us on March 29 for an information session about the planned Microsoft Malaga datacenter campus Datacenters provide the physical infrastructure for the technology we depend on at work and in our personal lives. Whenever you open an app on your phone, join a virtual classroom or meeting, snap and save photos, or play a game with your friends online, you are using a datacenter. Local businesses, government, hospitals, and schools rely on datacenters every day to deliver you goods and services. During this information session, you will have the opportunity to learn more about the planned datacenter that will be located on Malaga-Alcoa highway, understand our commitments to the community, review conceptual plans of the Malaga campus, and ask questions relating to the project. Event details: Wednesday, March 29, 2023 | Drop in between 6-8 p.m. Mission View Elementary School gymnasium, 60 Terminal Ave, Wenatchee, WA 98801 The event will be organized to accommodate English and Spanish. For more information about Microsoft’s work in Central Washington, visit the Microsoft in your community page . For community related questions, contact us at CentralWaDC@microsoft.com or leave a voicemail at 1-509-794-6526. For PR-related questions contact Microsoft Media Relations .

sources.excerpt: Westover Link datacenter construction update Microsoft is building a datacenter on Westover Link in San Antonio, Texas. Why datacenters are needed Datacenters provide the physical infrastructure for the technology we depend on at work and in our personal lives. Whenever you open an app on your phone, join a virtual classroom or meeting, snap and save photos, or play a game with your friends online, you are using a datacenter. Local businesses, government, hospitals, and schools rely on datacenters every day to deliver goods and services to you. Construction overview Microsoft and its general contractor, Walbridge have begun site clearing and excavation for the project. Our team is permitted for site clearing work through the City of San Antonio and will implement dust mitigation around the site. Together with the general contractor, Walbridge, we are committed to notifying the community of relevant updates during the construction project. Staying connected We will keep the community up to date via our “Microsoft in your community“ page at https://local.microsoft.com/texas . For construction related questions, please contact: Matt Haller (Project Manager) Email: Mhaller2@walbridge.com Cell: 313.350.3072 Community-related questions can be sent to texasDC@microsoft.com For PR-related questions, contact the Microsoft Media Relations at rapidresponse@we-worldwide.com

sources.name: Microsoft Heath datacenter construction updates
sources.excerpt: Heath datacenter construction updates Microsoft is building a datacenter in the City of Heath, Licking County. Why datacenters are needed Datacenters provide the physical infrastructure for the technology we depend on at work and in our personal lives. Whenever you open an app on your phone, join a virtual classroom or meeting, snap and save photos, or play a game with your friends online, you are using a datacenter. Local businesses, government, hospitals, and schools rely on datacenters every day to deliver goods and services to you. Construction update—July 2026 Summer activities underway at the Heath datacenter site Summer construction continues at the Microsoft datacenter site in Heath, with crews focused on safety, water management, and site preparation for future buildings. Work on the substation is also expected to begin. Residents may see fencing installed around portions of the site, stormwater holding ponds under construction, erosion controls maintained, and fill material brought in for grading. There will be an increase in truck traffic through the summer and fall, and crews will continue working to minimize impacts on neighboring properties. Microsoft appreciates the community’s continued support; questions or concerns can be directed to 380-267-4449 or info@msftheathdatacenter.com . Construction update—May 2026 As site preparation work continues, some Sunday work may be necessary to keep the project on schedule due to weather delays and time-sensitive construction milestones. Ames Construction remains in close communication with the City of Heath, which reviews and approves all work schedules and any temporary adjustments to permitted work hours. To receive advance notice of changes to work hours and other project updates, please send your email address to the project team at info@msftheathdatacenter.com . Construction update—March 2026 Site preparation begins at Heath datacenter site In the coming weeks, neighbors will see the initial activity on the site. Work will start with the removal of trees. Felled trees will be staged on site and processed with a woodchipper at a later time. Some logs may be removed from the site for reuse. Equipment used during tree removal will include chainsaws, large trucks, forestry-industry heavy equipment, and woodchippers. Crews will access the site using a construction entrance off Thornwood Drive. A second construction access road will be added off Lees Road in the near future. The tree removal activity is expected to last approximately one week, not counting the wood chipping at a later date. Early site preparation is anticipated to be substantially complete by the end of the year. A timeline for vertical construction has not yet been determined. We encourage neighbors to check back regularly for updates as work progresses. For questions or concerns, please contact the project team at 380-267-4449 or info@msftheathdatacenter.com . Construction update—February 2026 Microsoft has contracted Ames Construction as the general contractor for the Heath datacenter in Ohio. Mass grading construction is estimated to begin in February and completed in November 2026. Together with our general contractor Ames Construction, we will keep neighbors informed in advance of construction work. Completion of construction does not indicate datacenter operation/availability. Construction hours Permitted construction hours are Monday to Friday 7:00 AM – 7:00 PM with Saturdays and occasional Sundays from 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM. Staying connected We will keep the community up to date via our Ohio page on the Microsoft in Your Community blog . For construction related questions, email info@msftheathdatacenter.com or leave a message at 380-267-4449. For community-related questions, email us at ColumbusDC@microsoft.com or leave a message at 513-301-1414.

There will be an increase in truck traffic through the summer and fall, and crews will continue working to minimize impacts on neighboring properties. Microsoft appreciates the community’s continued support; questions or concerns can be directed to 380-267-4449 or info@msftheathdatacenter.com . Construction update—May 2026 As site preparation work continues, some Sunday work may be necessary to keep the project on schedule due to weather delays and time-sensitive construction milestones. For questions or concerns, please contact the Ames project team at (380) 222-6188 or email info@MSFTNewAlbanyDatacenter.com . Construction update—March 2026 After a quiet winter season, activity will increase at the New Albany datacenter site in the coming weeks as warmer weather allows work to resume. Beginning soon, soil will be delivered to the site via a designated truck route traveling along Highway 62 (Johnstown Road) to the site on Beech Road. The route may change to Jug Street instead of Highway 62 if there are unforeseen detours. Deliveries are scheduled Monday through Saturday for approximately 10 weeks. The soil will be used to build up designated areas of the site to meet plan specifications. Once grading is complete, seed will be planted as part of final stabilization efforts. Neighbors can expect to see large dump trucks and earth-moving equipment on and near the site. This is the final step in this phase of the project. When Ames Construction has completed the work, Microsoft will resume the lead role in project communications, and updated contact information will be shared. If you have questions or concerns, please contact the Ames project team at 380-222-6188 or email info@MSFTNewAlbanyDatacenter.com . Fall & Winter 2025 Construction Update As the seasons change, the focus at the New Albany datacenter site has shifted to preparing for the Ohio winter. Ames Construction continues site preparation, which will extend through spring 2026, with efforts centered on stabilizing the surface across the site. There will be a slight increase in truck traffic as soil is delivered to the site through the remainder of the year. Certain areas will require refinement during the spring; however, the completed stabilization efforts will enable winter and spring weather conditions to further bolster and reinforce the groundwork. A native seed mix has been sown across most of the site, with plans in place for seeding the remaining area along Beech Road. For questions about the project, contact us at (380) 222-6188 or email info@MSFTNewAlbanyDatacenter.com . Summer 2025 construction update Ames Construction continues with site preparation for the Microsoft datacenter in New Albany. Crews have begun building the foundation where the facilities will sit. For questions or concerns about the project, contact us at (380) 222-6188 or email info@MSFTNewAlbanyDatacenter.com . sources.name: Microsoft Conover – Lyle Creek datacenter construction update
sources.excerpt: Conover – Lyle Creek datacenter construction update Microsoft is building a datacenter in the greater Conover, North Carolina area near Highway 16 in Catawba County. Why datacenters are needed Datacenters provide the physical infrastructure for the technology we depend on at work and in our personal lives. Whenever you open an app on your phone, join a virtual classroom or meeting, snap and save photos, or play a game with your friends online, you are using a datacenter. Local businesses, government, hospitals, and schools rely on datacenters every day to deliver goods and services to you. September 2026: Construction update Work continues to move forward on the first building at the Lyle Creek datacenter site, with key milestones achieved on the building structure and exterior. The building exterior is in its final stages of completion. Framing and drywall work has started and continues to progress throughout the building. Work on underground infrastructure also continues to support the site and upcoming equipment deliveries. Mechanical and electrical work has begun, and additional interior work continues. Work is also beginning on additional building areas to support upcoming phases of construction. We appreciate the community’s patience as construction progresses and will continue to provide updates on significant milestones. May 2026: Construction update Work is advancing across multiple areas of the site, with key milestones reached in foundations and early structural development. Construction activity is moving forward as crews complete early phases and begin vertical construction: Underground work, foundations, and slab installation are complete for several buildings. Steel installation has begun on site, marking the start of above-ground construction. Additional buildings are progressing through foundation and footing stages as site-wide development continues. Telecommunications infrastructure work is underway in multiple areas to support future operations. February 2026: Construction update At the Lyle Creek site, Microsoft’s general contractor, Whiting‑Turner, will begin initial site preparation once weather conditions allow. Early activities will include installing fencing, preparing the site, and limited paving work to support temporary facilities. Foundation work is expected to begin in mid‑March, following completion of site preparation activities. Construction hours Construction activity is expected to take place from Monday to Friday, 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM. Work hours will follow local permitting requirements. May 2024: Construction timeline Datacenter construction began in March 2024. The general contractor Morgan Corp is preparing the site by excavating and crushing rock onsite. In some cases this involves controlled blasting in the early afternoon to break apart larger rocks. Together with our general contractor Morgan Corp we will keep neighbors informed in advance of construction work. Staying connected We will keep the community up to date via our North Carolina page in our Microsoft in your community blog. As of February 2026, our general contractor is Whiting-Turner. For construction related questions, please fill out this form, Lyle Creek Datacenter Campus . If you have any additional questions, please contact the Microsoft Community Affairs Manager at northcarolinadc@microsoft.com or leave a voicemail at 980-776-2251.

sources.excerpt: Mount Pleasant datacenter project update Project overview Microsoft is developing a datacenter campus in Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin. Why datacenters are needed Datacenters provide the physical infrastructure for the technology we depend on at work and in our personal lives. Whenever you open an app on your phone, join a virtual classroom or meeting, snap and save photos, or play a game with your friends online, you are using a datacenter. Local businesses, government, hospitals, and schools rely on datacenters every day to deliver goods and services to you. Construction update July 2026 As part of ongoing preparation at our datacenter site in Mount Pleasant, crews will begin moving soil materials between areas of the project site. Construction overview Starting on or around July 13, 2026, construction teams will begin hauling soil from one area of the site to another to support future development. This work is expected to continue for approximately eight weeks, depending on weather, permitting, and construction schedules. During this time, neighbors may notice: Increased truck traffic in and around the site. Movement of soil and construction materials. Stockpiling and early site preparation activity. Traffic and site operations Construction vehicles will use designated haul routes and approved access points within the project area. Teams will actively coordinate operations to help manage traffic flow and reduce impacts to the surrounding community. A map of the planned haul route is included for reference. Construction hours Construction activity will take place during permitted local construction hours. If work outside of these hours is required, it will follow all applicable local regulations. Staying connected We are committed to keeping our neighbors informed about construction activities. Questions about construction? Please contact Walsh Construction at MPDC@walshgroup.com or call 312-497-6967. Questions about other aspects of the project? Contact WisconsinDC@microsoft.com or leave a message at 608-535-3569. Learn more at local.microsoft.com/Wisconsin . June 2026: Community Connect Open House Microsoft hosted a Community Connect open house on June 23, 2026, at the Fountain Banquet Hall. The event provided an opportunity for community members to learn more about the Mount Pleasant datacenter project, hear the latest updates, and connect directly with subject matter experts. Attendees were able to ask questions and engage with project team members about ongoing construction activities, community investments, and upcoming milestones. Thank you to everyone who joined us and shared their feedback. Boards for Mount Pleasant Community Connect Open House April 2026: Community Office Hours Microsoft hosted “community office hours” for neighbors of the Mount Pleasant datacenter on April 9, 2026, at the Mount Pleasant Village Hall Ebe Auditorium. The informal session provided an opportunity for community members to hear about Mount Pleasant datacenter project updates, ask questions, and learn more about local investments and job opportunities. Thank you to everyone who participated. For those who were unable to attend, a link is available to view the presentation materials shared during the session. Boards for Mount Pleasant community office hours Construction update March 2026 Construction overview Construction continues at the Mount Pleasant Datacenter Campus , with progress underway across multiple phases. Phase 1—KR & 90th Work in this phase is nearing completion. Crews are finalizing interior work in several buildings and completing landscaping. Construction for Phase 1 is anticipated to be complete by spring 2026 . Phase 2—KR & H Construction activities for Phase 2 are ongoing and focused on expanding the site. Current work includes foundation installation, steel erection, and underground utility installation. This phase is scheduled to be completed in early 2028 . Phase 3—Durand & Hewitt Memorial Drive Preliminary earthwork is underway to prepare the site for future construction. To support construction operations, there are currently four site entrances: Gate 1: Highway KR Gate 2: Braun Road Gate 3: County Road H Gate 4: County Road H Construction schedule and activity Work is expected to begin in mid March , depending on ground conditions as seasonal thaw continues. To help reduce dust and debris on nearby roads, street sweepers will operate for approximately 10 hours per day . Tire wash systems are also in place at site exits to help keep surrounding roadways clean. Construction hours Construction activities are conducted in compliance with the Village of Mount Pleasant code. Work may take place between 6 AM and 10 PM, seven days per week . We appreciate your continued patience and cooperation as our crews move into the next phase of construction. Walsh Construction remains committed to minimizing disruption and maintaining safe, clean roadways throughout the project. Questions about construction? sources.excerpt: newly rebuilt deck for a resident during the United Way of Richmond County's annual Days of Caring. Amazon is building a new data center campus in Richmond County, North Carolina, but the team didn't wait for operations to begin to start getting involved. From September 16–18, 45 employees fanned out across the county for the United Way of Richmond County's annual Days of Caring, volunteering on three projects and logging nearly 170 hours combined. Feeding kids on the weekends The team spent the morning with Backpack Pals, assembling more than 450 weekend meal kits for children across Richmond County schools. The kits make sure students have something to eat when the cafeteria isn't an option. Many of our employees are parents, so this project was personal. Making Ms. Vickie's home accessible again Part of the team joined Habitat for Humanity of the NC Sandhills for a multiday volunteer effort to demolish and rebuild three decks for Ms. Vickie, a local resident who could no longer safely get in and out of her home. Our team was proud to be part of the crew that made her home accessible again. Getting the food pantry ready The rest of the team deep-cleaned and restocked Our Daily Bread Food Ministry's food pantry from floor to ceiling—organizing shelves, rotating inventory, and preparing it to serve the families who depend on it most. sources.excerpt: Ginger East datacenter construction update Microsoft is building a datacenter in greater Des Moines, Iowa. Why datacenters are needed Datacenters provide the physical infrastructure for the technology we depend on at work and in our personal lives. Whenever you open an app on your phone, join a virtual classroom or meeting, snap and save photos, or play a game with your friends online, you are using a datacenter. Local businesses, government, hospitals, and schools rely on datacenters every day to deliver goods and services to you. Construction overview Microsoft has contracted Weitz Construction as the general contractor for the Ginger East datacenter in Iowa. Construction is estimated to be completed by mid-2028. Together with our general contractor Weitz Construction, we will keep neighbors informed in advance of construction work. Completion of construction does not indicate datacenter operation/availability. Construction hours Permitted construction hours are: 6 AM – 6 PM Mon-Fri 6 AM – 3:30 PM Sat, Sun, Holidays Staying connected We will keep the community up to date via our Greater Des Moines page in our Microsoft in Your Community blog. For PR-related questions, contact the Microsoft Media Relations at rapidresponse@we-worldwide.com

sources.name: Microsoft Silver Springs datacenter construction update
sources.excerpt: Silver Springs datacenter construction update Microsoft is beginning early construction work at its datacenter site in Silver Springs, Nevada. We are committed to keeping the community informed as work progresses and to reducing construction-related impacts where possible. Why datacenters are needed Datacenters provide the physical infrastructure that supports the technology people use every day. Microsoft datacenters support online services that enable communication, remote work, learning, healthcare, business operations, and other digital activities. Construction overview Construction update September 2026 Early construction activities have started at the Silver Springs site. Current work includes preparing the property, moving earth, and relocating utility lines. Community members may notice trucks entering and leaving the site, construction equipment operating on the property, and occasional drone surveys above the work area. Microsoft and its contractor will take steps to control dust and stagger truck traffic to help reduce impacts on nearby roads and the surrounding community. Q&D Construction LLC is the general contractor for this work. Construction is expected to continue through several stages over the next few years. Construction hours Construction follows legally permitted work hours and is generally scheduled during the following times: Monday through Friday: 7 AM to 7 PM Saturday: 9 AM to 5 PM Sunday and city holidays: No work scheduled Staying connected Microsoft and Q&D Construction LLC welcome questions about construction activities. Community members may contact the construction team at: Email: outreachrno18@qdconstruction.com Phone: 775-353-7030 We appreciate the community’s patience while this work is underway and will provide additional updates as construction progresses. > >> >> … … … …

sources.name: Microsoft Alviso datacenter construction update
sources.excerpt: Alviso datacenter construction update Alviso datacenter construction begins in California Microsoft is expanding its datacenter infrastructure with construction at our new Alviso site in California. This update marks the beginning of a multi-phase effort to prepare the land for future datacenter development, supporting the growing demand for cloud services and digital transformation. Why datacenters are needed Datacenters provide the physical infrastructure for the technology we depend on at work and in our personal lives. Whenever you open an app on your phone, join a virtual classroom or meeting, snap and save photos, or play a game with your friends online, you are using a datacenter. Local businesses, government, hospitals, and schools rely on datacenters every day to deliver goods and services to you. Construction overview HITT Contracting Inc. is the general contractor for the Alviso datacenter. Construction began in fall 2025 with initial work focused on earthmoving and soil remediation. Site preparation work is expected to be completed by summer 2026. We’re working closely with HITT to keep neighbors informed ahead of any major construction activity. Construction hours Work will take place Monday through Friday, from 7:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Should additional hours be required, HITT will adhere to the local requirements. Staying connected We’re committed to keeping the community informed. Visit our Microsoft in your community page for updates.

sources.excerpt: Port Washington, Wisconsin Data Center Port Washington Data Center Facts Open all Jobs The Port Washington project is expected to generate more than 4,000 union construction jobs and more than 1,000 ongoing project-supported jobs onsite. Local suppliers, vendors, contractors and residents will be prioritized with a union-first approach. Community Impact The project will contribute $175 million for local infrastructure upgrades, including expanded capacity for water and wastewater treatment facilities, upgraded water mains and sewer lines, a new water tower and power infrastructure. It’s expected to generate more than $11 billion for the local economy. Additional initiatives will focus on restoring wetlands, increasing biodiversity, and minimizing light pollution. Energy 70% of energy for the Port Washington campus will come from zero-emission sources, including wind, solar, and batteries. The project will add about 2,000 MW of new zero-emission power to Wisconsin’s grid, which means more reliable, affordable energy for local families and businesses. The project will fully fund all electrical infrastructure upgrades, requiring no increase to local energy bills. Water The Port Washington AI data center uses a closed-loop, non-evaporative liquid cooling system that significantly reduces water consumption. There’s a commitment to being “water positive,” with restoration projects returning more water to the environment than the campus consumes. Size The campus will consist of four buildings on 500 of its 672 acres. Remaining acres will be preserved as natural spaces. Interested in a Career at an Oracle Data Center? sources.name: Microsoft Jacksonville datacenter project updates
sources.excerpt: Jacksonville datacenter project updates Microsoft is building a datacenter on Jacksonville Avenue in Manassas, Virginia. Why datacenters are needed Datacenters provide the physical infrastructure for the technology we depend on at work and in our personal lives. Whenever you open an app on your phone, join a virtual classroom or meeting, snap and save photos, or play a game with your friends online, you are using a datacenter. Local businesses, government, hospitals, and schools rely on datacenters every day to deliver goods and services to you. September 2024: Construction updates In September 2024, Lemartec began rock removal as part of the preparation work on Jacksonville Avenue in Manassas. Earthworks include excavating and crushing rock. We anticipate completion by early 2025. We appreciate your patience as Lemartec crews work to safely construct this new datacenter. January 12, 2024: Site preparation update In January 2024, Microsoft’s general contractor, Lemartec, began site preparation work on Jacksonville Avenue in Manassas. Lemartec is permitted by Prince William County to work between 6 am and 10 pm Monday through Friday and between 9 am and 10 pm on Saturdays, Sundays and some holidays. We anticipate this phase to be completed mid-2024. We appreciate your patience as Lemartec crews work to safely construct this new datacenter. Staying connected For more information about Microsoft’s work in Northern Virginia, visit the Microsoft in your Community, Northern Virginia page. https://local.microsoft.com/communities/americas/northern-virginia/ For construction related issues, please contact Lemartec’s project manager, David Duret dduret@lemartec.com or 786-580-8428 for emergencies. For PR-related questions, email rapidresponse@we-worldwide.com If you have any additional questions, please contact Microsoft Community Engagement: CQ-NVA-Datacenters@microsoft.com or leave a voicemail at 703-657-1760.

sources.name: Microsoft Ginger West datacenter construction update
sources.excerpt: Ginger West datacenter construction update Microsoft is building a datacenter in greater Des Moines, Iowa. Why datacenters are needed Datacenters provide the physical infrastructure for the technology we depend on at work and in our personal lives. Whenever you open an app on your phone, join a virtual classroom or meeting, snap and save photos, or play a game with your friends online, you are using a datacenter. Local businesses, government, hospitals, and schools rely on datacenters every day to deliver goods and services to you. Construction overview Microsoft has contracted Turner Construction as the general contractor for the Ginger West datacenter in Iowa. Construction is estimated to be completed by summer 2028. Together with our general contractor Turner Construction, we will keep neighbors informed in advance of construction work. Completion of construction does not indicate datacenter operation/availability. Construction hours Permitted construction hours are: 6 AM – 6 PM Mon-Fri 6 AM – 3:30 PM Sat, Sun, Holidays Staying connected We will keep the community up to date via our Greater Des Moines page in our Microsoft in Your Community blog. For construction related questions, please contact Project Manager (PM): Rebecca Kalinowskyr , Turner Construction. For community related questions, contact us at iowadc@microsoft.com and 425-705-2709. For PR-related questions, contact the Microsoft Media Relations at rapidresponse@we-worldwide.com

Beginning in 2027, Amazon’s facility in Canton will transition entirely to using recycled wastewater for cooling, reusing an average of 83 million gallons annually. Amazon data centers: How much water and electricity do they really use? Data centers create new jobs, use significantly less water than golf courses and car washes, and don't drive up electricity rates. Supporting local communities Amazon volunteers and community members assembling meal kits in Jackson, Mississippi. sources.name: Microsoft Palmetto datacenter construction update
sources.excerpt: Palmetto datacenter construction update Microsoft began constructing the Palmetto datacenter in April 2024. The datacenter construction site is located in the Greater Atlanta area of Palmetto, GA. Why datacenters are needed Datacenters provide the physical infrastructure for the technology we depend on at work and in our personal lives. Whenever you open an app on your phone, join a virtual classroom or meeting, snap and save photos, or play a game with your friends online, you are using a datacenter. Local businesses, government, hospitals, and schools rely on datacenters every day to deliver goods and services to you. Recap: Palmetto Datacenter Project Information Session On July 23, 2024, Microsoft, in collaboration with the Mayor of Palmetto, hosted an initial information session at Palmetto Elementary School to discuss the datacenter project. The purpose of the meeting was to inform residents about the project’s details, including operations, construction activities, and community investments. Participants viewed the site plans, visual renderings, and had the opportunity to speak with the project team. If you were unable to attend, you can view materials shared , below and access video clips of the meeting. For more information or to share feedback, contact: georgiadc@microsoft.com Materials shared at the information session on July 23, 2024 View from Johnson Rd. Secondary entrance High level construction timeline Microsoft Datacenter Academy is coming to Atlanta Learn more Construction timeline Datacenter construction began in April 2024 and is estimated to be complete by the beginning of October 2025. The general contractor Turner Construction Company is permitted to work Monday through Saturday 7:00am – 7pm, excluding federal holidays. Staying connected We will keep the community up to date via our Greater Atlanta page in our Microsoft in Your Community blog. For daily operational questions, you can also reach out to the contractors: Project Manager – Jason Padavich DBIA, LEED GA at jpadavich@tcco.com Senior Project Manager – Jim Buckner at jbuckner@tcco.com Project Superintendent – Todd R. Cooksey at tcooksey@tcco.com For Microsoft specific inquiries: PalmettoDC@Microsoft.com
